description: Write a Python ETL script (lxml or xml.etree + pandas) for retail_chain that converts namespaced purchase-order XML documents into a line-level Parquet table. The script should: (1) parse with namespace-aware lookups, (2) emit one row per line element with a 1-based line_no, carrying order id, currency and order date from the parent, (3) read sku and qty from attributes and price and the optional note from child elements, (4) emit a single row with null line fields for orders that have no line elements so that order counts are preserved, (5) cast qty to nullable Int64 and price to decimal(10,2).

source_columns.xml_document: string (namespace urn:example:po; order[@id, @currency] > date, line[@sku, @qty] > price, note?)

edge_cases: Element lookups without the namespace (find('order')) return nothing and yield an empty output with no error
PO-2 has no lines and must still produce one row
The entity & must be decoded to '&' in the note
Attribute values are strings; qty must be cast to an integer type that tolerates nulls
A missing optional note element yields null, not the string 'None'
common_failure_modes: FM5: Namespace-unaware parsing silently produces zero rows
FM1: Orders without child lines dropped during flattening
FM7: No check that the number of distinct orders in the output equals the number of order elements
